controls.description: HR issues a leaver notification to payroll on or before the employee's last working day, and payroll confirms removal from the payroll master before the next pay run.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Signed leaver checklist; payroll master change log showing the removal date.
controls.limitations: Can be bypassed by collusion between HR and payroll; ineffective if the notification step is skipped under time pressure.
controls.objective: Ensure terminated employees are removed promptly so no further payments are processed.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: An independent person reconciles the payroll master headcount to HR employment records each pay period and investigates differences.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Signed reconciliation with documented follow-up of differences.
controls.limitations: Only as good as the HR records it is compared against; will not detect collusion that falsifies both sides.
controls.objective: Detect ghost or terminated employees remaining on the payroll.
controls.responsible_role: Finance manager, independent of payroll processing
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Payroll master changes (new starters, leavers, pay rate and bank detail changes) require independent approval before they take effect.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Approved change request forms or system workflow approvals; audit trail of changes.
controls.limitations: Can be overridden by management; ineffective against collusion between the requester and the approver.
controls.objective: Prevent unauthorised or fictitious changes to employee master data.
controls.responsible_role: HR manager / finance manager, independent of payroll processing
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: System access rights segregate payroll master maintenance from payroll payment processing and release, and access rights are reviewed periodically.
controls.evidence_of_operation: User access rights report; periodic access review signed off by management.
controls.limitations: Access reviews may be perfunctory; privileged IT users may bypass application-level controls.
controls.objective: Prevent one person from both creating a payee and paying them.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Overtime is approved in advance (or promptly afterwards) by a supervisor independent of the claimant, based on operational need.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Approved overtime claim forms or system approval records.
controls.limitations: Supervisors may approve routinely without real scrutiny; does not detect collusion between claimant and supervisor.
controls.objective: Ensure only genuine, necessary overtime is paid.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: An exception report of overtime by employee and department is reviewed periodically and unusual patterns are investigated.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Reviewed exception report with investigation notes and sign-off.
controls.limitations: Review may be high-level; effectiveness depends on defined thresholds and genuine follow-up.
controls.objective: Detect excessive or anomalous overtime claims.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Payroll rate tables, tax tables and deduction parameters are updated from authoritative sources, and changes are independently reviewed before the pay run.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Updated parameter tables with reviewer sign-off; change log.
controls.limitations: Reviewer may not verify the source of the parameters; configuration errors in the payroll system may not be visible in the tables.
controls.objective: Ensure payroll is calculated from correct, current rates and parameters.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: The payroll summary is independently reviewed and reconciled to the general ledger before payments are released.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Reviewed and signed payroll summary; payroll-to-GL reconciliation.
controls.limitations: A high-level review may not detect systematic calculation errors affecting all employees equally.
controls.objective: Detect calculation errors and ensure payroll agrees with the accounting records.
controls.responsible_role: Finance manager, independent of payroll processing
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: HR leaver lists or vouching results identifying payees who are not current employees.
evidence.description: The detailed payroll listing per pay period showing each payee, gross pay, deductions and net pay, reconciled to the bank payment file.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Complete per pay period; footed; agreed to the bank payment total; payees identifiable.
evidence.limitations: Internally generated; proves what was paid, not that each payee was a genuine employee.
evidence.name: Payroll register (payroll summary)
evidence.reliability_notes: Reliability depends on payroll controls. Where leaver or segregation controls are weak, the register is the population under test rather than corroboration of occurrence.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Payroll master still showing a listed leaver as active after the termination date.
evidence.description: The HR-maintained list of employees who left employment in the period, with last working dates.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Complete for the period; last working dates stated; maintained by HR independent of payroll.
evidence.limitations: Incomplete if HR is not notified of all departures; can be manipulated if HR colludes with payroll.
evidence.name: HR leavers list (termination register)
evidence.reliability_notes: More reliable where HR is independent of payroll processing and leaver paperwork is filed promptly; weakened where notification is informal or delayed.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Employment files that are thin, inconsistent, or created after the audit inquiry.
evidence.description: HR files evidencing current employment: appointment letters, contracts, identification, and recent attendance or appraisal records.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Complete file per employee; consistent dates and terms; current supervisor identifiable.
evidence.limitations: Files can be fabricated; inspection looks for internal consistency but cannot prove authenticity alone.
evidence.name: Employment records (HR files)
evidence.reliability_notes: Contracts and identification documents are more persuasive than informal records. Reliability increases when files are maintained by HR independent of payroll and show a history consistent with the claimed employment.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Change requests approved only by the person who entered the change.
evidence.description: System-generated log of all additions and amendments to the payroll master (new starters, leavers, rate and bank detail changes), showing who made each change and when.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Complete for the period; user and timestamp per change; before/after values visible.
evidence.limitations: Only records changes made through the system; privileged users may be able to alter or delete the trail.
evidence.name: Payroll master change audit trail
evidence.reliability_notes: System-generated trails are more reliable than manual logs, provided privileged users cannot alter them. Reliability is highest where the auditor extracts the trail directly.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Actual system permissions differing from the report (e.g. shared administrator logins).
evidence.description: Report of system users and their payroll permissions, showing who can maintain master data and who can process or release payments.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Current as at the extraction date; covering all payroll roles; identifying privileged accounts.
evidence.limitations: Reflects a point in time only; does not show historical access during the period under audit.
evidence.name: User access rights report
evidence.reliability_notes: More reliable where extracted by the auditor directly from the system. A point-in-time report cannot prove segregation held throughout the period, so it is combined with change-trail testing.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Master changes with no matching approved request.
evidence.description: Documented requests to change payroll master data, with independent approval signatures or workflow approvals.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Identifiable change, requester and independent approver, dated before the change took effect.
evidence.limitations: An approval signature proves a step was performed, not that the approver genuinely reviewed the change.
evidence.name: Approved payroll change requests
evidence.reliability_notes: Reliability depends on the independence of the approver from the requester and on evidence that approval preceded the change.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Attendance records or production logs contradicting the claimed overtime hours.
evidence.description: Employee overtime claim forms or timesheets showing hours claimed, with supervisor approval.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Hours stated per day; claimant and independent approver identified; dated.
evidence.limitations: Self-reported hours; approval may be perfunctory.
evidence.name: Overtime claim forms / timesheets
evidence.reliability_notes: Inquiry-level evidence on its own; reliability comes from independent approval and corroboration to attendance or production records.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Overtime claims for days the employee was recorded absent.
evidence.description: Independent records of attendance (clocking data, shift rosters) or production output that can corroborate hours worked.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Independently maintained; covering the overtime dates; reconcilable to claimed hours.
evidence.limitations: System-generated clocking data can be manipulated by buddy-punching; production records may not map neatly to hours.
evidence.name: Attendance / production records
evidence.reliability_notes: More reliable where maintained independently of the claimant (e.g. electronic clocking). Corroborates the occurrence of overtime but not its operational necessity.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Exception report showing the same employees flagged repeatedly with no investigation.
evidence.description: System or manual report highlighting overtime above thresholds, by employee and department.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Thresholds defined; all exceptions listed; review sign-off and investigation notes.
evidence.limitations: Only flags what exceeds the threshold; systematic small-scale inflation may not appear.
evidence.name: Overtime exception report
evidence.reliability_notes: Reliability depends on complete input data and evidence of genuine review; an unreviewed report is not evidence of control operation.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Contracts or salary schedules showing different rates from those used in the payroll run.
evidence.description: Authoritative sources for pay: employment contracts, approved salary schedules, and statutory tax and deduction tables in force for the period.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Current for the period; approved; traceable to an authoritative source.
evidence.limitations: A contract proves the agreed rate, not that the rate was entered correctly into the payroll system.
evidence.name: Authorised pay rates and statutory tables
evidence.reliability_notes: External statutory tables are highly reliable for the correct parameters; internal salary schedules are reliable only where independently approved.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: General ledger payroll balances that do not agree with the payroll register.
evidence.description: Payroll-related general ledger accounts (wages expense, tax payable, other deductions payable) for the period.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Reconciled postings per pay period; journals identifiable.
evidence.limitations: Agreement proves the payroll was posted, not that it was calculated correctly.
evidence.name: General ledger payroll accounts
evidence.reliability_notes: Auditor-performed reconciliation increases reliability for completeness of posting; does not address calculation accuracy.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Whether payroll is material; how leavers are communicated to payroll and how quickly; whether anyone reconciles the payroll master to HR records; who can add or remove payees.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where payroll is material. Less applicable where the owner or a senior manager personally reviews every payee each period, or where a small, stable workforce makes every payee known to management - in those cases the opportunity is sharply reduced.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: payroll occurrence testing routinely targets ghost employees where leaver controls are weak.
factor_risk.explanation: A lag between termination and removal from the payroll master creates a window in which payments can continue. Because bulk electronic payments are processed without payee-by-payee review, continued payments may go unnoticed, overstating payroll expense and diverting cash. The factor indicates a control deficiency and a possibility to test - it does not prove any payment was improper.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Payroll is processed in-house or via bulk bank file, and there is no reliable evidence that leavers are removed from the payroll master before the next pay run.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Who can amend the payroll master and who releases payments; whether system access rights enforce segregation; whether master changes are independently approved; whether the payroll payment file is reviewed before release.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies wherever access rights combine master maintenance with payment processing, regardless of entity size. Less applicable where system-enforced segregation exists and master changes require a second approver - the mapping then addresses the residual risk of collusion or override rather than the single-person opportunity.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice and control frameworks: segregation of incompatible duties is a fundamental control over payroll fraud.
factor_risk.explanation: Segregation of duties is the primary control against creating a fictitious payee and paying them. When one person controls both the master record and the payment, the fraud can be executed and concealed in a single step, leaving no independent record to detect it. This is a control deficiency that creates opportunity; it is not evidence that fraud has occurred.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: One person can both change employee master data and process or release payroll payments without independent approval or review.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Whether overtime is material; how overtime hours are recorded (self-reported vs independently clocked); who approves overtime and how; whether overtime is compared to production or attendance records.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where overtime is material or paid at premium rates. Less applicable where overtime is rare, immaterial, or independently clocked with automatic supervisor alerts - the opportunity for unapproved claims is then limited.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: unapproved overtime is a classic payroll leakage tested through vouching and analytical procedures.
factor_risk.explanation: Without independent approval, there is no check that overtime was worked or was necessary. Self-reported hours can be inflated and paid automatically, particularly where supervisors approve routinely. The factor creates opportunity and removes detection; whether any claim was actually inflated must be established by testing.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Overtime hours claimed by employees are paid without review or approval by a supervisor independent of the claimant.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Whether payroll is calculated manually or by system; how rate and tax tables are updated and reviewed; whether the payroll summary is independently reviewed before payment; volume of correcting journals.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where payroll calculations involve manual inputs, frequent rate changes, or complex deductions. Less applicable where a well-controlled outsourced payroll provider calculates pay and the entity only reviews outputs - the risk then shifts to the review control and the service organisation.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: recalculation of payroll is a standard substantive procedure where calculation controls are weak.
factor_risk.explanation: Incorrect rates, outdated tax tables or misconfigured deductions flow directly into every affected employee's pay and into the related liabilities. Because the error is systematic, it can be material in aggregate even where each individual error is small. Identifying the factor means calculation accuracy must be tested, not that any specific payment is wrong.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Payroll inputs, rates, tax tables or deduction parameters are entered or maintained without independent verification.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where payroll is material and leaver processing is manual or spread across HR and finance without a coordinated checklist. Relevant where bank payments are made by electronic file that is not reviewed payee-by-payee.
factors.description: Former employees (resigned, dismissed, retired or deceased) are not removed from the payroll master in a timely manner, so payroll continues to process payments against their records.
factors.name: Employees remain on the payroll after leaving employment
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Headcount per payroll register exceeds HR headcount; payroll cost trends upward while reported headcount is flat or falling; payments to employees with no current work location or supervisor; leaver paperwork filed but the payroll master unchanged.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where payroll master maintenance and payment processing are not segregated, whether in a manual system or through broad system access rights.
factors.description: One individual can add or amend employee master records (new starters, bank details, pay rates) and also process or release payroll payments, with no independent check.
factors.name: Employee records and payroll payments are controlled by the same person
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: A single user holds administrator access to the payroll system; master changes with no approval trail; payroll amendments processed close to pay run deadlines; the same person handles leavers, new starters and bank payments.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where overtime is material or paid at premium rates, and where timesheets are self-reported rather than independently clocked.
factors.description: Overtime hours claimed by employees are paid without review or approval by a supervisor independent of the claimant.
factors.name: Overtime is not independently approved
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Overtime concentrated in a few employees; overtime spikes before period-end; overtime claims without corresponding production records; supervisors approving their own team's overtime without review.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where payroll involves manual inputs, frequent rate changes, complex deductions, or a newly implemented or reconfigured payroll system.
factors.description: Payroll is calculated using incorrect pay rates, tax tables or deduction parameters, whether through manual error, outdated tables or system configuration errors.
factors.name: Payroll calculations are incorrect
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Employee complaints about pay; frequent correcting journals to payroll; tax filings inconsistent with payroll records; payroll processed under time pressure with manual adjustments.

procedure_evidence.notes: Payroll summaries are the data analysed.
HR headcount is the independent comparator.
Leavers list is the starting population.
Payroll register confirms whether the leaver was paid after termination.
Payees are selected from the payroll register.
Employment files are the evidence vouched to.
Leaver checklists are inspected for the control test.
Access report is directly inspected.
Change trail is the population sampled.
Change requests are the approval evidence vouched to.
Register provides the recorded amounts recalculated.
Authorised rates are the independent inputs to the recalculation.
New starters and bank changes are extracted from payroll data.
Employment files corroborate that new starters are genuine.
Timesheets are the documents vouched.
Attendance records corroborate hours claimed.
Overtime cost data is analysed.
Exception report is the focus of the analysis.
Approved hours are the recalculation input.
Authorised overtime rates are the recalculation input.
Approval signatures are inspected on the claim forms.
Register provides the recorded net pay recalculated.
Authorised rates and tables are the independent inputs.
Contracts and schedules are the authorised sources agreed to.
Payroll register is reconciled to the ledger.
GL accounts are the other side of the reconciliation.
Payroll cost and headcount data are analysed.

procedures.exception_criteria: Unexplained cost increases; headcount per payroll materially exceeding HR records; departments with cost growth but no headcount growth.
procedures.expected_result: Payroll cost movements are consistent with headcount changes and explained by valid causes (pay rises, headcount changes).
procedures.follow_up: Drill into the affected department's payees; vouch a sample of employees to HR records; if ghost employees are indicated, extend procedures to quantify the overpayment and assess fraud risk indicators without presuming fraud.
procedures.objective: Identify departments or periods where payroll cost is inconsistent with headcount, indicating possible payments to non-employees.
procedures.population: Monthly payroll summaries and headcount reports for the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Not sampling - trend analysis over the full period.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain monthly payroll summaries and HR headcount reports for the period.
Compare payroll cost and headcount by department to prior periods and to budget.
Investigate departments where cost rises without corresponding headcount growth, or where payroll headcount exceeds HR headcount.
procedures.title: Analyse payroll cost trends by department and headcount

procedures.exception_criteria: Leavers paid after their last working day; leavers still active in the master; final pay unsupported.
procedures.expected_result: Each leaver is removed from the payroll master before the next pay run; final pay is correctly calculated and supported.
procedures.follow_up: Quantify overpayments; investigate the cause; test whether overpaid amounts were recovered; consider extending testing to the full leaver population.
procedures.objective: Verify that terminated employees stop being paid after their last working day.
procedures.population: All employees who left in the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Sample across months and departments; extend to a census if exceptions are found.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain the HR leavers list for the period, with last working dates.
For a sample of leavers, inspect the payroll master to confirm the removal date precedes the next pay run.
Inspect the final pay calculation for each sampled leaver and agree it to the last working date.
procedures.title: Trace leavers to removal from the payroll master

procedures.exception_criteria: Payees with no employment file; payees whose HR record shows termination; duplicate or suspicious bank account details shared between unrelated payees.
procedures.expected_result: Each sampled payee is a current employee supported by valid employment evidence, with bank details agreeing to HR records.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate each exception with HR; quantify payments to the affected payees; evaluate fraud risk indicators - do not automatically conclude fraud; consider reporting obligations under professional standards.
procedures.objective: Confirm that individuals paid through payroll are genuine current employees.
procedures.sampling_notes: Risk-based sample: include employees with no supervisor on record, recent bank detail changes, and round-sum net pay.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Select a sample of employees from the payroll register.
Vouch each to an HR employment file: appointment letter or contract, identification, and evidence of current employment (recent attendance, current supervisor).
Agree the bank account paid against the bank details held in the HR file.
procedures.title: Vouch a sample of payees to current employment evidence

procedures.exception_criteria: Missing checklists; unsigned or late leaver notifications; removals processed after a further payment.
procedures.expected_result: Checklists are complete, signed and dated; removals occur before the next pay run.
procedures.follow_up: Control exceptions are control deficiencies, not proof of misstatement. Assess the deficiency and increase substantive procedures over leavers and payees accordingly.
procedures.objective: Test whether the leaver notification and removal control operates as designed.
procedures.sampling_notes: Sample across the period; include months with high leaver volumes.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Select a sample of terminations from the HR leavers list.
Inspect the leaver checklist for HR and payroll sign-off and dates.
For one case, reperform the check that removal preceded the next pay run.
procedures.title: Inspect the leaver-to-payroll process

procedures.exception_criteria: Users combining master-change and payment-release rights; access reviews missing, unsigned, or not followed up.
procedures.expected_result: No user combines incompatible duties; access reviews are performed and exceptions followed up.
procedures.follow_up: Treat as a control deficiency; do not conclude misstatement from access rights alone. Expand substantive procedures over master changes and payments for the period the weakness existed.
procedures.objective: Determine whether system access enforces segregation between maintaining employee records and processing payments.
procedures.population: Payroll system users and access rights.
procedures.sampling_notes: Census of users with payroll permissions.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain the payroll system user access report (extracted directly where possible).
Identify users holding both master-change and payment processing or release rights.
Inspect the most recent periodic access review for evidence of performance and follow-up.
procedures.title: Inspect payroll system access rights

procedures.exception_criteria: Unapproved changes; changes supported only by the person who entered them; bank detail changes without independent verification.
procedures.expected_result: Each sampled change is approved by an independent person before taking effect and supported by HR documentation.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate the business purpose of each unapproved change; trace the related payments; quantify any overpayment; evaluate fraud indicators without presuming fraud.
procedures.objective: Verify that changes to employee master data are authorised and genuine.
procedures.population: All payroll master changes in the period (from the audit trail).
procedures.sampling_notes: Risk-based sample: all bank detail changes and new starters; sample of rate changes.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Extract the audit trail of payroll master changes for the period.
Select a sample, covering all bank detail changes and new starters.
Vouch each change to an approved change request and to supporting HR documentation (appointment letter, contract amendment).
procedures.title: Vouch master changes to independent approval

procedures.exception_criteria: Differences in rates, hours or deductions; bank details differing from HR records.
procedures.expected_result: Recalculated gross pay, deductions and net pay agree with the payroll register.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate whether differences indicate error or manipulation; if a pattern emerges, extend testing and reconsider the risk assessment.
procedures.objective: Verify the accuracy of payroll calculations for a sample of employees.
procedures.population: Payroll register for a selected pay period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Sample across pay grades and departments; include employees with recent master changes.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Select a sample of employees from a recent pay run.
Independently recalculate gross pay, statutory and other deductions, and net pay from authorised rates and inputs.
Agree the bank details paid against the bank details in the HR file.
procedures.title: Reperform the payroll calculation for a sample of employees

procedures.exception_criteria: Employees sharing bank accounts; new starters with incomplete files; bank detail changes clustered just before pay runs.
procedures.expected_result: All new starters and bank detail changes correspond to genuine employment events with complete documentation.
procedures.follow_up: Vouch the anomalies to employment evidence; investigate with HR; if fictitious employees are indicated, quantify payments and assess fraud risk indicators without presuming fraud.
procedures.objective: Identify anomalous new payees or payment redirections indicative of fictitious employees.
procedures.population: New starters and bank detail changes in the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Full-population scan for anomalies; targeted vouching of exceptions.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain lists of new starters and bank detail changes for the period.
Scan for anomalies: shared bank accounts, incomplete files, PO box or residential addresses inconsistent with the role, changes just before pay runs.
Vouch anomalies to HR employment evidence and approval records.
procedures.title: Analyse new starters and bank detail changes

procedures.exception_criteria: Overtime paid without approval; approved hours differing from attendance records; overtime claimed by employees recorded as absent.
procedures.expected_result: Sampled overtime payments are supported by approved timesheets and corroborated by attendance records.
procedures.follow_up: Quantify unapproved or uncorroborated overtime; investigate with supervisors; if the pattern is systemic, extend testing and consider the control deficiency in the risk assessment.
procedures.objective: Verify that paid overtime was actually worked and independently approved.
procedures.sampling_notes: Risk-based sample: highest overtime earners and departments with spikes.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Select a sample of overtime payments, weighted toward the highest earners.
Vouch each to the underlying timesheet and to independent supervisor approval.
Agree claimed hours to attendance or production records for the same dates.
procedures.title: Vouch overtime payments to approved timesheets

procedures.exception_criteria: Overtime concentrated in a few employees without operational justification; spikes inconsistent with production levels.
procedures.expected_result: Overtime patterns are consistent with operational needs and production levels; exceptions are explained.
procedures.follow_up: Vouch unexplained exceptions to timesheets and approvals; investigate with operational management.
procedures.objective: Identify unusual overtime patterns indicative of inflated claims.
procedures.population: Overtime cost by employee and department for the period and comparatives.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Analyse overtime cost and hours by employee and department, compared to prior periods.
Identify concentrations, spikes and employees whose overtime is disproportionate to their role.
Corroborate explanations against production or activity records.
procedures.title: Analyse overtime trends and exceptions

procedures.exception_criteria: Overtime paid at incorrect rates; hours paid differing from approved hours.
procedures.expected_result: Recalculated overtime pay agrees with amounts paid.
procedures.follow_up: Determine whether differences are isolated errors or systematic; quantify and propose adjustment if material.
procedures.objective: Verify overtime is calculated at the correct rates.
procedures.population: Overtime payments in a selected pay period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Sample covering different overtime rate bands.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Select a sample of overtime payments.
Independently recalculate overtime pay from approved hours and the authorised overtime rates.
Investigate differences.
procedures.title: Recalculate overtime pay

procedures.exception_criteria: Claims paid without independent approval; approvals by the claimant's subordinate or peer.
procedures.expected_result: Overtime claims show timely approval by an independent supervisor.
procedures.follow_up: A missing approval is a control deficiency, not proof the overtime was not worked. Increase substantive vouching of unapproved claims.
procedures.objective: Test whether the overtime approval control operates as designed.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Select a sample of overtime claims.
Inspect each for approval by a supervisor independent of the claimant, dated before or promptly after payment.
Note any self-approved or missing approvals.
procedures.title: Test the overtime approval control

procedures.exception_criteria: Recalculated amounts differ from the register; outdated tax tables used; deductions omitted or miscalculated.
procedures.expected_result: Recalculated gross pay, deductions and net pay agree with the payroll register.
procedures.follow_up: Determine whether errors are isolated or systematic; if systematic, quantify the aggregate effect on wages expense and statutory liabilities and consider the compliance implications.
procedures.objective: Verify payroll calculations are mathematically correct and based on current parameters.
procedures.population: Payroll register for selected pay periods.
procedures.sampling_notes: Sample across pay grades; include employees with complex deductions.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Select a sample of employees from recent pay runs.
Independently recalculate gross pay, each deduction (tax, social security, other) and net pay using the authorised rates and the statutory tables in force.
Compare with the payroll register and investigate differences.
procedures.title: Recalculate net pay for a sample of employees

procedures.exception_criteria: Rates in the payroll system differing from contracts or salary schedules; unauthorised rate changes.
procedures.expected_result: Pay rates used agree with authorised contracts or salary schedules.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate unauthorised rates; quantify the effect; determine whether the change indicates error or manipulation.
procedures.objective: Verify that pay rates in the payroll system are authorised.
procedures.population: Pay rates in the payroll master.
procedures.sampling_notes: Sample across grades; include all recent rate changes.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Select a sample of employees, including all recent pay rate changes.
Agree the rate in the payroll master to the employment contract or approved salary schedule.
Inspect approval for each rate change.
procedures.title: Agree pay rates to authorised sources

procedures.exception_criteria: Unexplained reconciling items; payroll journals posted directly to the ledger bypassing the payroll summary.
procedures.expected_result: The payroll register reconciles to the general ledger; reconciling items are valid and explained.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate unreconciled differences; quantify the potential misstatement of wages expense and related liabilities.
procedures.objective: Confirm payroll postings to the ledger are complete and agree with the payroll register.
procedures.population: Payroll register totals and general ledger payroll accounts for each pay period.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Reperform the reconciliation of the payroll register totals to the general ledger payroll accounts for each pay period.
Investigate and obtain explanations for reconciling items.
Verify that year-end payroll accruals are supported and correctly measured.
procedures.title: Reconcile payroll to the general ledger and investigate differences

procedures.exception_criteria: Average cost per head moving inconsistently with known pay rises or headcount changes; unexplained jumps in a single period.
procedures.expected_result: Average payroll cost per head is consistent with headcount changes, pay rises and the mix of employees.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate unexplained movements by drilling into the underlying payees and rates.
procedures.objective: Corroborate overall payroll reasonableness against headcount and known pay changes.
procedures.population: Aggregate payroll cost and headcount for the period and comparatives.
procedures.sampling_notes: Not applicable - analytical review of aggregates.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Calculate average payroll cost per head by department for the current and comparative periods.
Compare movements with known pay rises, headcount changes and overtime trends.
Investigate inconsistencies.
procedures.title: Analytical review of payroll cost per head

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where the payroll register is the primary record of wage expense; tested by vouching payees to current employment evidence.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: If payments continue after termination, the recorded payroll transactions include payments that did not represent genuine employment costs - the transactions did not occur as bona fide payroll.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant only where payroll accruals or unpaid wages are material at the reporting date; otherwise the balance-sheet effect is through the cash outflow already recorded.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: If ghost employees remain in the payroll master at the reporting date, accrued wages or payroll-related payables may include obligations that do not exist.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where the individual could create new payees; tested by vouching payees and master changes to independent employment evidence.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Fictitious employees, or payments diverted through manipulated bank details, are recorded as genuine payroll transactions that did not occur as legitimate employment costs.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where the individual can amend rates or payment details; tested by recalculation and agreement of rates to authorised sources.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Inflated pay rates or altered payment details change the amounts paid, so recorded payroll amounts are inaccurate even for real employees.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where overtime is claimed on self-reported timesheets without independent approval.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Overtime claimed but not worked, or not independently verified, means recorded overtime transactions did not occur as genuine labour cost.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where premium overtime rates apply and hours are manually entered; tested by recalculation.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Inflated hours or incorrect premium rates make the recorded overtime amounts inaccurate.

risk_assertions.conditions: Central to this risk; tested by independent recalculation from authorised rates and current statutory tables.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Incorrect rates, outdated tax tables or misconfigured deductions directly produce inaccurate recorded payroll amounts.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant only where payroll-related accruals (unpaid wages, bonuses, tax payable) are material at the reporting date; calculation errors carry through to the accrual.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Systematic calculation errors also misstate the related period-end accruals, since the accrual is derived from the same incorrect parameters.

risk_controls.explanation: Directly addresses the factor by closing the gap between termination and removal from the payroll master.
Detects ghost or terminated employees that the preventive control missed, by comparing two independent populations.
Removes the single-person opportunity by requiring a second person to authorise master changes.
System-enforced segregation prevents one user from holding both sides of the incompatible duties.
Independent approval is the primary check that overtime was worked and necessary.
Detects patterns of inflated overtime that individual approvals might miss.
Ensures the parameters feeding the calculation are correct and current.
Independent review of the payroll summary before payment provides a last chance to detect calculation errors.

risk_procedures.reason: Analytical scan to identify departments or periods where cost is inconsistent with headcount - the first indicator of ghost payees.
Directly tests whether leavers stop being paid, tracing from the independent HR population.
Vouching payees to employment evidence is the primary occurrence test for ghost employees.
Tests whether the leaver removal control operates, to determine the extent of substantive work needed.
Directly tests the factor: whether access rights allow one person to combine the incompatible duties.
Tests whether master changes - the mechanism for creating fictitious payees - are independently authorised.
Recalculation detects inflated rates or manipulated payment details.
Anomaly analysis targets the classic indicators of fictitious employees: shared bank accounts and incomplete files.
Vouching overtime to approved timesheets and attendance records is the primary occurrence test.
Analytical procedures identify concentrations and spikes that individual vouching might miss.
Recalculation verifies the accuracy of overtime at premium rates.
Tests whether the approval control the factor says is missing actually operates.
Independent recalculation is the direct test of calculation accuracy.
Verifies the rates feeding the calculation are authorised.
Confirms calculated payroll is completely and accurately posted, including year-end accruals.
Analytical review corroborates overall payroll reasonableness and highlights systematic errors.

risks.causes: Leaver notifications not communicated from HR to payroll; no periodic reconciliation between the payroll master and HR employment records; bulk electronic payments processed without payee-by-payee review.
risks.description: Wages, allowances or termination-related payments continue to be processed for individuals who have left employment, diverting funds and overstating payroll costs.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases with payroll size, staff turnover and electronic bulk payments. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists - it identifies a possibility the auditor must test, not a finding.
risks.potential_consequences: Payroll costs and related liabilities are overstated; cash is diverted to unauthorised recipients; statutory deductions on ghost pay may create compliance issues.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Payments to ghost or terminated employees

risks.causes: No segregation of duties between master maintenance and payment processing; excessive system access rights; no independent approval of master changes; no review of the payroll payment file before release.
risks.description: An individual with combined custody of employee records and payments could create fictitious employees, inflate pay rates, alter bank details, or process duplicate payments, diverting cash.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases where one person has end-to-end control and where payments are released without review. The factor describes a control deficiency that creates opportunity; it does NOT prove that fraud or misstatement has occurred.
risks.potential_consequences: Payroll expense overstated; cash diverted to unauthorised recipients; bank detail changes misdirect legitimate pay.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Fictitious employees created or pay details manipulated

risks.causes: No independent approval of overtime; self-reported timesheets; no comparison of overtime to production or attendance records.
risks.description: Employees may claim overtime not worked, or record excessive hours, and the amounts are paid without detection, overstating payroll costs.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases where overtime is material, paid at premium rates, and self-reported. The absence of approval does NOT prove any claim was inflated - each claim must be tested.
risks.potential_consequences: Payroll costs overstated; inequitable or fraudulent payments; budget overruns in labour-intensive operations.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Inflated or fictitious overtime payments

risks.causes: Outdated tax tables; manual rate entry errors; incorrect payroll system configuration; unauthorised rate changes.
risks.description: Systematic or isolated errors in pay rates, tax calculations or deductions cause wages, tax liabilities and related balances to be misstated.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases with manual processing, frequent rate changes and complex deductions. Identifying this factor means calculation accuracy must be tested; it does NOT prove that any specific payment is wrong.
risks.potential_consequences: Wages expense misstated; statutory liabilities (tax, social security) misstated with compliance consequences; employee relations issues.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Payroll expense and deductions misstated through calculation errors

rules.name: Terminated employees remain on payroll -> ghost employee risk
rules.rationale: A lag between termination and removal from the payroll master, combined with bulk electronic payments, creates the opportunity for continued payments to non-employees. The rule directs occurrence-focused testing: analytical scans, tracing leavers, and vouching payees to employment evidence.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: Whether payroll is material to the financial statements.
How leavers are communicated from HR to payroll, and the typical delay before removal.
Whether anyone reconciles the payroll master to HR employment records.
then.note: Ghost-employee testing starts from independent populations (HR leaver lists, headcount) rather than from the payroll register itself, which is the record under suspicion.

rules.name: No segregation of payroll duties -> fictitious payee risk
rules.rationale: Combined control of employee master records and payment processing removes the primary barrier to creating fictitious payees. The rule directs the auditor to test access rights, vouch master changes to independent approval, and scan for fictitious-employee indicators.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: Which users hold payroll master-change and payment-release rights.
Whether master changes require independent approval in the system or on paper.
Whether the payroll payment file is reviewed before release.
then.note: Access rights alone do not prove misstatement; they establish opportunity. Substantive testing of master changes and payments is required to determine whether the opportunity was exploited.

rules.name: Overtime not independently approved -> inflated overtime risk
rules.rationale: Without independent approval there is no check that overtime was worked or necessary, particularly where hours are self-reported. The rule directs vouching of overtime to approved timesheets corroborated by attendance records, plus analytical procedures to find concentrations.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: Whether overtime is material, and at what premium rates it is paid.
How overtime hours are recorded - self-reported timesheets or independent clocking.
Who approves overtime and whether approval is independent of the claimant.
then.note: A missing approval is a control deficiency, not proof the overtime was not worked. Unapproved claims require heavier substantive vouching, not automatic disallowance.

rules.name: Incorrect payroll calculations -> misstated wages and deductions
rules.rationale: Errors in rates, tax tables or deduction parameters flow systematically into pay and related liabilities. The rule directs independent recalculation from authorised sources, agreement of rates, and reconciliation of payroll to the ledger.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: Whether payroll is calculated manually, by system, or by an outsourced provider.
How rate and tax tables are updated, and whether changes are independently reviewed.
Whether the payroll summary is independently reviewed before payments are released.
then.note: Because calculation errors are often systematic, the auditor quantifies the aggregate effect on wages expense and statutory liabilities rather than treating each error as isolated.
